sources.institution: United Nations Economic Commission for Africa
United Nations Economic Commission for Africa

evidence.estrutura: Songwe is an economist and development-policy leader rather than a constitutional theorist. Her work favors capable national and regional institutions without a specific centralization-versus-federalism doctrine.
evidence.representacao: Her governance work emphasizes institutional reform, policy accountability and inclusive development, supporting democratic-quality institutions without a specific electoral-system program.
evidence.poder: Macroeconomic reform, governance and institutional accountability are central to her work. This supports rule-bound state capacity rather than arbitrary executive power.
evidence.imigracao: Her regional African development work is cross-border and integration-oriented, but the reviewed sources do not establish a specific immigration or assimilation doctrine.
evidence.diplomacia: Senior UN, World Bank and regional roles strongly support multilateral cooperation and international economic diplomacy.
evidence.intervencao: Her agenda focuses development finance, institutions, trade and cooperation rather than military policy. This supports a restrained non-military orientation.
evidence.economia: Her World Bank, IFC and ECA career supports market-based development, private-sector growth, macroeconomic stability and public investment. This is a market-oriented developmental mixed economy.
evidence.controle: She favors fiscal and institutional reform, investment frameworks and public policy rather than command planning. Use low-to-moderate economic control.
evidence.comercio: Trade, competitiveness and African regional integration are explicit priorities in her ECA work, strongly supporting open and integrated regional trade.
evidence.religiao: Her professional public agenda is secular and technocratic. No evidence supports religious governance.
evidence.moral: Her development work addresses poverty, inequality and inclusive growth, supporting moderate egalitarian social values without a broad cultural-policy agenda.
evidence.tecnologia: Digital transformation is explicitly listed among the priorities she brought to ECA. This strongly supports a pro-technology and digital-development orientation.
